p6.tat-modell-eller-moe.1: Dense model or Mixture of Experts
p6.tat-modell-eller-moe.2: In an MoE model, the MLP in each layer is replaced by many smaller MLPs (experts) and a router. Attention is still dense.
p6.tat-modell-eller-moe.3: Each token is sent to top-k experts. So the model carries a lot of knowledge (many parameters) at a low cost per token (few active).
p6.tat-modell-eller-moe.20: Memory is set by the total: all experts must sit in GPU memory. The compute per token is set by the active ones.
p6.routern.2:
r = h @ W_router        W_router [4096, E]
                        r [T, E]
top-k index per token
g = softmax(r[top-k])   [T, k]
out = Σ g · Expert(h)   [T, 4096]
p6.routern.3: The router is just a small linear matrix, trained together with the rest. Nobody tells it what the experts should know.
p6.routern.4: Specialization varies with model, layer and training data. Mixtral often showed syntactic patterns such as indentation and punctuation rather than clear topic experts. This does not rule out topic-related specialization in other models. A load balancing loss encourages more even use but does not guarantee balance in every batch.
p6.routern.5: Each layer has its own experts and its own router. A token takes its own path through all the layers.

p6.moe-i-inferens.2: Small batches: each token reads only its own experts’ weights. Decode gets fast, almost like a model the size of the active parameters.
p6.moe-i-inferens.3: Large batches: different tokens pick different experts, and soon all of them are in use. Then all the weights get read again, and the advantage lies in the compute, not the memory.
p6.moe-i-inferens.4: Expert parallelism: the experts are spread across GPUs. Each token is sent to the right GPU (all-to-all dispatch) and the results are sent back (combine). That is a lot of communication, so fast links between the GPUs matter.
p6.moe-i-inferens.5: Imbalance: if many tokens pick the same expert, one GPU becomes the bottleneck while the others wait.
p6.attention-varianter.2: MHA: one KV head per query head. Largest cache.
p6.attention-varianter.3: GQA: groups of query heads share KV (Llama 3, Mistral, Qwen).
p6.attention-varianter.4: MQA: a single KV head for all of them.
p6.attention-varianter.5: MLA (DeepSeek-V2/V3): K and V are compressed into a latent vector that gets cached, and unpacked when needed.
p6.attention-varianter.6: Sliding window: some layers only see the most recent W tokens, so their logical cache stops growing. Gemma 2 alternates local and global layers 1:1; Gemma 3 uses 5:1.
p6.attention-varianter.7: The comparison uses 32 layers and d = 4096 for all variants, to isolate the effect of the attention variant itself.
p6.lang-kontext.2: Two things grow with the context:
p6.lang-kontext.3: The KV cache grows linearly with global attention. With these shapes and bf16, 128000 tokens use about 16.78 GB (15.625 GiB); 131072 tokens (128K) use 16 GiB. This is within Llama-3.1’s context, not Llama-3’s original 8192.
p6.lang-kontext.4: The attention computation per token grows linearly, and for a whole prefill quadratically.
p6.lang-kontext.5: The chart shows what share of the computation per generated token goes to attention, versus context length. With short prompts it is negligible. At 128K it dominates.
p6.lang-kontext.6: Longer context can require changed RoPE frequencies and continued training. Position interpolation and YaRN are different methods. Llama 3.1 uses its own frequency-dependent scaling, not YaRN: low frequencies are scaled down, high frequencies retained and the middle range blended. With continued training the context was extended from 8192 to 131072 tokens.
p6.resonerande-modeller.2: The architecture is the same. The difference is that the model has been trained with RL to write out a long reasoning before the answer, often inside tags like <think>…</think>.
p6.resonerande-modeller.4: Almost all the time goes to decode, which is the most expensive phase per token.
p6.resonerande-modeller.5: The KV cache grows with the reasoning, so fewer sequences fit at the same time.
p6.resonerande-modeller.6: max_tokens has to cover both the thinking and the answer.
p6.resonerande-modeller.7: vLLM can split the output into reasoning and answer with --reasoning-parser.
p6.resonerande-modeller.8: This is also where loops hurt: a model that repeats itself burns decode steps until it hits the ceiling.
p6.multimodala-modeller.2: An image is split into patches, run through a vision encoder (usually a ViT) and projected to the same width d as the language model’s residual stream. The result is inserted into the sequence where a placeholder token stood.
p6.multimodala-modeller.3: After that, image tokens are ordinary positions in the stream: they get K and V in the cache and can be attended to like any word.
p6.multimodala-modeller.4: Example: LLaVA-1.5 splits a 336 × 336 pixel image into 14 × 14 patches, which gives 576 image tokens. So images are expensive in both prefill and KV memory.
p6.multimodala-modeller.5: vLLM runs the encoder separately and caches its output so the same image is not encoded twice.
p6.andra-arkitekturer.2: Decoder-only (GPT, Llama): causal mask, generates text. The focus of this course.
p6.andra-arkitekturer.3: Encoder-only (BERT): every token sees all the others. Produces good vectors for classification and embeddings, but does not generate.
p6.andra-arkitekturer.4: Encoder-decoder (T5, Whisper): an encoder reads the input, a decoder generates and reads the encoder via cross-attention.
p6.andra-arkitekturer.5: SSM and hybrids (Mamba, Jamba): a fixed-size state replaces the growing KV cache. Linear time in sequence length. Hybrids mix in a few attention layers so they do not lose precision.
p6.testa-dig-sjalv.2: Mixtral 8x7B has 46.7 B parameters. How much GPU memory do the weights need in bf16, and how much does each token compute?
p6.testa-dig-sjalv.3: About 93 GB for the weights, because all experts have to be in memory. The compute per token matches a dense model of about 13 B.
p6.testa-dig-sjalv.4: Why does MoE give less benefit with large batches than with small ones?
p6.testa-dig-sjalv.5: With small batches only the weights of the chosen experts are read. With large batches the tokens together pick almost all the experts, so all the weights get read anyway.
p6.testa-dig-sjalv.6: Which attention variant gives the smallest KV cache: GQA with 8 KV heads or MLA?
p6.testa-dig-sjalv.7: MLA: 576 numbers per token and layer, versus 2 · 8 · 128 = 2048 for GQA-8 with d_h 128.
p6.testa-dig-sjalv.8: What does an image cost in a LLaVA-1.5-like model, counted in tokens?
p6.testa-dig-sjalv.9: 576 positions in the sequence, with as much KV cache as 576 text tokens.

p6.attention-sinks-och-lokal.2: Full attention looks at every earlier position. That makes prefill quadratic in T and lets the KV cache grow linearly with the context — 128 KiB per token in Llama-3-8B.
p6.attention-sinks-och-lokal.3: Many newer models mix local and global layers, but the ratio varies. The following hypothetical 28/4 example keeps the other Llama-3-8B shapes and bf16, with 28 local and 4 global layers. It is not a Llama, Gemma or gpt-oss configuration. Quality must be evaluated, not assumed unchanged.
p6.attention-sinks-och-lokal.4:
Llama-3-8B, all layers global     128 KiB/token
28 layers in a 4,096 window       112 KiB × min(T, 4,096)
4 global layers                    16 KiB/token
p6.attention-sinks-och-lokal.5: At 32000 tokens the fully global comparison costs about 3.91 GiB per sequence, while the hypothetical 28/4 example needs about 0.93 GiB. The 28 local layers attend to at most 4096 positions per token, not the whole context. This is memory arithmetic, not support for 32000 tokens in the original Llama-3-8B.
p6.attention-sinks-och-lokal.6: Three variants you meet in practice:
p6.attention-sinks-och-lokal.7: Local window: every token only sees the last w tokens (Mistral, 4,096).
p6.attention-sinks-och-lokal.8: Mixed local/global: Gemma 2 and gpt-oss alternate 1:1; Gemma 3 uses 5:1 (local:global layers).
p6.attention-sinks-och-lokal.9: Attention sinks: the first tokens always stay in the cache, because the model uses them as a dumping ground for attention (StreamingLLM).
p6.attention-sinks-och-lokal.10: The baseline Llama-3-8B has only global layers and an 8192 context. Longer sequences in the memory comparison are hypothetical, or require a long-context model such as Llama-3.1. For hybrid models count KV cache layer by layer; actual memory savings also depend on the engine’s cache management.
